newsitem.title: BRAZIL: COOL EARLY TEMPS, NO FROST FOR BRAZIL COFFEE-SOMAR.
newsitem.headline: COOL EARLY TEMPS, NO FROST FOR BRAZIL COFFEE-SOMAR.

text.p: Brazilian coffee regions should see cool early mornings and hot, sunny afternoons in the coming days with no forecasts of frosts, local meteorologists Somar said on Monday.
Minimum temperatures in the last 24 hours ranged between four and nine degrees Celsius in Pocos de Caldas, Minas Gerais, traditionally Brazil's coldest coffee region.
The cool temperatures are due to the tail-end of a polar air mass which has left the country.
Another weak cold front will pass through the southeast region between August 12-13 but the associated air mass will only affect the far south of the country before heading out to sea, Somar said.
"The coming morning will see the same kind of early morning temperatures, then it should warm up on August 13 and then cool again slightly on August 14," said Somar forecaster Marcos Massari.
"But minimum temperatures will not fall below current levels, there will be no problems. The threat of frost is now over for this year," he added.
